answer: Sybil fleets exploit one weakness: a design cheap to replicate. Close it with a cost that is per-identity, non-transferable, paid in real resources. Let each identity's eligibility be a mesa of peer-verified work: standing rises only through attested service, can't be purchased or inherited, erodes if unattended. Bind admission to a keyed proof-of-work from a fresh random source, so one solve can't be replayed across a jetty of clones. Hold part of each stake in a vault that unlocks only to its own key after real epochs — the attacker pays compute, time, and locked capital per fake.
